stories.title: CBRE Arranges Sale of Fully Renovated San Diego Business Park
stories.excerpt: CBRE arranged the $26.5-million sale of 5&52 Business Park, a 71,597-square-foot industrial property located at 5965 and 5975 Santa Fe St.in San Diego. San Diego-based Parallel Capital Partners and Boston-based Long Wharf Capital sold the property to Sukut Real Properties. CBRE’s Hunter Rowe, Matt Carlson, Mike Longo and Matt Pourcho represented the sellers. “5&52 Business Park offered a compelling opportunity to acquire a fully leased and repositioned coastal industrial asset,” said Rowe, a senior vice president at CBRE. “The transaction reflects how San Diego’s defense industry is evolving. Investors are focused on assets where next-generation defense technology tenants are driving innovation and growth.” Originally constructed in the 1980s, the property was acquired completely vacant in 2025 and fully renovated with new roofs, skylights, LED lighting, HVAC, modern office buildouts, warehouse upgrades, exterior improvements and electrical and plumbing upgrades. The property was subsequently fully leased to Seasats and Applied Intuition. The post CBRE Arranges Sale of Fully Renovated San Diego Business Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sukut Real Properties acquired 71,597 SF industrial asset in San Diego for $26.5M.
Property fully leased to defense-tech tenants Seasats and Applied Intuition post-renovation.
Investor focus on next-gen defense technology drives coastal San Diego industrial demand.
stories.summary: Parallel Capital Partners and Long Wharf Capital sold 5&52 Business Park, a fully renovated 71,597-square-foot industrial property in San Diego, to Sukut Real Properties for $26.5 million. The asset was acquired vacant in 2025, comprehensively upgraded, and fully leased to defense-tech tenants. The transaction reflects investor appetite for coastal industrial assets tied to next-generation defense innovation.
stories.impact: San Diego's defense-tech cluster is driving industrial real estate demand and valuations in the coastal submarket. Multifamily developers should monitor co-location dynamics: defense-tech job growth and high-wage employment concentration in San Diego will sustain and attract resident populations, strengthening rental demand for apartments near these employment corridors.

stories.title: Heisman Headquarters, and Trophies, Coming to 120 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Silverstein Properties has secured a new office lease with Heisman, keeper of the Heisman Trrophy. The charitable organization will relocate its headquarters to 5,000 square feet on the 13th floor of 120 Broadway in 2027. As part of a 10-year agreement, Heisman will display two of the famed Heisman Memorial Trophies, awarded annually since 1935 to the most outstanding college football player in the U.S., at Silverstein’s Downtown Manhattan tower. One will be placed on public display in the lobby and the other in The Landmark, the building’s 10th-floor amenity center. Heisman will also rebrand a section of The Landmark as the Heisman Lounge. “120 Broadway is a celebrated landmark, which makes it the perfect home for the legendary Heisman Trophy,” said Silverstein Properties SVP of leasing, Joe Artusa. “We are pleased to welcome Heisman – an established Downtown organization whose employees will benefit from 120 Broadway’s prime location, expansive amenities and high-end service.” Silverstein Properties was represented in-house by Artusa, along with Erik Harris of Newmark. Michael Norris of Cushman & Wakefield represented Heisman. The post Heisman Headquarters, and Trophies, Coming to 120 Broadway appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Heisman Trophy organization leases 5,000 SF at 120 Broadway Downtown Manhattan for 10 years.
Silverstein Properties secures anchor tenant; trophy on public display drives foot traffic.
Office lease signals Downtown Manhattan demand resilience and amenity-driven tenant attraction.
stories.summary: Silverstein Properties secured a 10-year, 5,000-square-foot office lease with the Heisman Trophy organization at 120 Broadway in Downtown Manhattan, with occupancy in 2027. The organization will display two Heisman Trophies—one in the lobby and one in a rebranded Heisman Lounge on the 10th floor—as part of the agreement.
stories.impact: Low impact for multifamily. This is an office leasing win for Downtown Manhattan but does not signal material job growth, population influx, or cost/supply shifts affecting residential demand. Heisman is a small, specialized tenant with modest employment footprint.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Close Sale of Western Massachusetts Dental Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap has closed the sale of a five-property dental office portfolio consisting of dental condominiums and a freestanding dental office building located throughout the Pioneer Valley region of Western Massachusetts. The portfolio sold for $5.95 million. “The mix of dental condominiums and freestanding buildings made this a unique transaction, as some investors can be hesitant to pursue condominium assets,” said Kobe Gaskin, associate investments. “Ultimately, the buyers recognized the value of having an established national dental operator occupying these locations and the long-term stability that specialized medical properties can provide.” Gaskin, Billy Skoch and Chris Mitchel, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Cleveland office, in association with Thomas Shihadeh, Marcus & Millichap’s Massachusetts broker of record, marketed the property on behalf of the seller. The portfolio was acquired by two separate buyers, one based locally and the other based in Utah. The post Marcus & Millichap Close Sale of Western Massachusetts Dental Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap closed $5.95M sale of five-property dental office portfolio in Western Massachusetts.
Mix of condominiums and freestanding buildings; sold to local and Utah-based buyers.
Established national dental operator occupancy provides long-term stability and investor appeal.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of a five-property dental office portfolio in the Pioneer Valley region of Western Massachusetts for $5.95 million. The portfolio included dental condominiums and a freestanding dental office building, with a mix of buyer profiles (local and Utah-based). The transaction was anchored by an established national dental operator, providing revenue stability.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Specialized medical office assets and their valuations do not materially influence apartment demand, supply, or cost structure in Western Massachusetts. No signal of population migration or employment growth affecting residential markets.

stories.title: Metro Services Group Elevates Jacqueline Korajkic to CEO
stories.excerpt: Metro Services Group, a national provider of janitorial and engineering services with a concentrated presence in California and the Pacific Northwest, announced that Jacqueline Korajkic will become CEO effective Jan. 1, 2027. She succeeds founder and CEO Michael Oddo, who will remain chairman of the board of the company he founded over 30 years ago. Company President Derek Schulze will continue in his role. “Jacqueline has been central to Metro’s development for nearly a decade, and she has earned this opportunity through the breadth of her accomplishments,” said Oddo. “She understands the financial side of the business, but just as importantly, she understands our operations, our people and our clients. She is involved in virtually every aspect of growing the company.”  Korajkic joined Metro in 2018 as an accountant and rose through the organization to CFO. Much of her work happened behind the scenes, building the technology, people and financial foundations that support Metro’s leaders and clients. She also played a central role in facilitating Metro’s ownership transition to an employee stock option plan. The post Metro Services Group Elevates Jacqueline Korajkic to CEO appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Metro Services Group promotes Jacqueline Korajkic to CEO effective January 1, 2027.
Company operates janitorial and engineering services concentrated in California and Pacific Northwest.
Founder Michael Oddo remains chairman; leadership transition signals operational maturity and growth phase.
stories.summary: Metro Services Group announced that Jacqueline Korajkic will become CEO on January 1, 2027, succeeding founder Michael Oddo, who will remain chairman. Korajkic joined the company in 2018 as an accountant, rose to CFO, and oversaw technology, financial, and operational infrastructure development. The transition reflects organizational growth and succession planning.
stories.impact: Not relevant to multifamily development. Metro Services Group is a facilities management company with no direct bearing on apartment demand, supply, capital availability, or construction costs in California and the Pacific Northwest.

stories.title: Post-Election Tech Selloff May Hit Properties Linked to AI
stories.excerpt: Thursday’s massive sell-off of technology stocks following resounding Republican losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections reverberated throughout the artificial intelligence industry, but it is too soon to determine whether a number of commercial real estate properties could also be caught up in the political crosshairs, market insiders said. The tech-dominated Nasdaq stock index tumbled 5.52 percent Thursday two days after the Democrats seized control of Congress and downballot measures curbing data center development succeeded, leaving the fate of many of those projects up in the air. Following Thursday’s bloodbath, the Nasdaq was down more than 10 percent from a record high achieved on Oct. 6, 2026, before recovering 1.09 percent on Friday. Suhail Tayyeb, a professor at the New York University Schack Institute of Real Estate, stressed that any material hits that may face office owners who have heavy exposure to AI tenants will take time to sort out. “A stock market sell-off doesn’t automatically translate into weaker commercial real estate leasing,” Tayyeb said. “The impact depends on whether companies change their hiring, expansion plans or capital commitments.” There were certainly no signs of any AI leasing slowdown in New York City this week. Ten AI firms toured various office buildings in Midtown South both before and after Election Day, according to a source. The AI interest in the Big Apple includes SpaceX looking at 300,000 square feet, Palantir exploring leasing 400,000 square feet, and Sierra interested in leasing 250,000 square feet, according to sources. Anthropic is also looking to expand in Manhattan beyond the 465,530-square-foot lease it signed at 330 Hudson Street in April. Tayyeb noted that the 2000 dot-com collapse and the 2022 tech correction both contributed to weaker leasing and increased sublease availability, but those effects played out over time rather than overnight. bullets: Nasdaq fell 5.52% Thursday; tech stock selloff follows post-election political shift favoring data center restrictions.
Downballot measures curbing data center development succeeded; AI infrastructure projects face regulatory headwinds.
Office leasing impact on AI-tenant properties unclear; market effects on CRE require time to materialize.
stories.summary: Following Republican losses in midterm elections, a technology stock selloff saw the Nasdaq tumble 5.52% as downballot measures restricting data center development succeeded. The tech and AI sectors face regulatory uncertainty, with data center project timelines and financing at risk. Experts note that stock market declines do not automatically translate to weaker CRE leasing or occupancy.
stories.impact: Tech-heavy office markets (San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, Austin) face headwind: AI infrastructure constraints may slow enterprise hiring and expansion, dampening office leasing demand and indirectly softening demand for apartments near tech campuses. Multifamily developers should reassess underwriting assumptions for tech-adjacent submarkets and expect slower job-driven population growth in AI hubs over the next 12–18 months.

stories.title: Lincoln, McCourt Launch 344-Unit Culver City Mixed-Use
stories.excerpt: Lincoln Property Company and McCourt Partners have broken ground for ElevenOneEleven, a new mixed-use development in Culver City. The groundbreaking occurred three weeks after Lincoln and McCourt announced $133 million in construction financing from Bank OZK. Set to rise on a vacant parcel, ElevenOneEleven will deliver 344 rental apartments, including 52 affordable units, along with 2,000 square feet of retail and 17,520 square feet of publicly accessible outdoor space. “Culver City remains one of the strongest rental markets in Southern California, and this site captures many of the qualities that make the location compelling, including proximity to major employers, necessity serving retail and convenient access to the best West LA lifestyle amenities,” said Stephen Lindgren, SVP and Los Angeles market lead at Lincoln. ElevenOneEleven marks Lincoln’s third Culver City development and adds to its multifamily pipeline of more than 2,200 residential units underway across Los Angeles County. The post Lincoln, McCourt Launch 344-Unit Culver City Mixed-Use appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lincoln Property and McCourt broke ground on ElevenOneEleven in Culver City with $133M Bank OZK financing.
Development delivers 344 apartments (52 affordable), 2,000 SF retail, 17,520 SF public space.
Culver City identified as strong rental market with proximity to major employers and West LA amenities.
stories.summary: Lincoln Property Company and McCourt Partners broke ground on ElevenOneEleven, a mixed-use development in Culver City, California, three weeks after securing $133 million in construction financing from Bank OZK. The project will deliver 344 apartments (including 52 affordable units), 2,000 square feet of retail, and 17,520 square feet of publicly accessible outdoor space on a vacant parcel.
stories.impact: Culver City continues to demonstrate strong rental fundamentals and market appeal for institutional multifamily capital; proximity to employers and West LA lifestyle amenities support sustained rent growth. Lincoln's third Culver City project and 2,200-unit pipeline across LA County signal confidence in Los Angeles metro fundamentals and available financing despite macro uncertainty. Increased supply in Culver City will absorb local demand but may pressure rents if market-wide absorption falters.

stories.title: Atlas Capital Group Buys 360 West 43rd Street Apartments for $143M
stories.excerpt: An entity of the Brodsky Organization has offloaded its multifamily property at 360 West 43rd Street in Manhattan’s Hell’s Kitchen neighborhood. The purchase price was $142.5 million, according to a source familiar with the deal. The 256-unit development on 43rd Street between Eighth and Ninth avenues was sold off-market to Atlas Capital Group, the real estate investment and management firm announced on Friday. Ivan Hakimian of HPNY was involved in the off-market transaction, but declined to comment on the deal. A spokesperson for Atlas also declined to provide further transaction details, and Brodsky’s office did not respond to a request for comment. The 23-story building two blocks west of Times Square was acquired and developed by 42/9 Residential, a Brodsky entity, in 2002, according to city records. The property spans 250,000 square feet, including 13,000 square feet of ground-floor commercial space and a parking garage. There are currently no available units in the building, according to StreetEasy. The most recently signed lease was for a $3,795-per-month studio, signed in August, according to the apartment-hunting platform. Acquisition of the West 43rd Street property adds to Atlas Capital’s expanding multifamily portfolio, the firm said in a statement, which includes 15 Park Row in Lower Manhattan, 80 DeKalb in Downtown Brooklyn and the Denizen in Brooklyn’s Bushwick. Atlas kick-started 2026 with the $112 million purchase of 250 East Houston Street, a 130-unit mixed-use building in Manhattan’s East Village, from Dermot Company and Rockwood Capital, CO reported in January. Atlas is in the midst of co-developing luxury condominiums at 80 Clarkson Street in the West village, as well as senior affordable housing at nearby 570 Washington Street. It’s also entered into a partnership to develop an Upper West Side residential tower at 200 West 97th Street. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Atlas Capital Group acquired 256-unit Hell's Kitchen apartment at 360 West 43rd Street for $142.5M.
Property 100% occupied; 23-story building with 13,000 SF ground-floor commercial and parking garage.
Manhattan multifamily sustains pricing and buyer demand despite broader office distress in Midtown.
stories.summary: Atlas Capital Group purchased 360 West 43rd Street, a 256-unit apartment building in Manhattan's Hell's Kitchen, for $142.5 million in an off-market transaction from the Brodsky Organization. The 23-story property, developed in 2002, is currently 100% occupied and includes 13,000 square feet of ground-floor commercial space and a parking garage. No units are available according to StreetEasy.
stories.impact: Hell's Kitchen and West Midtown Manhattan multifamily markets remain resilient and attractive to institutional capital despite office sector stress elsewhere in Manhattan. Strong occupancy and off-market deal flow signal sustained rent power in residential-focused neighborhoods. Developers should note that multifamily in lifestyle/amenity-rich areas near transit outperforms office-adjacent submarkets; Hell's Kitchen's residential/retail/hospitality mix supports demand even as nearby office towers struggle.

stories.title: Bushburg in Contract to Buy 60 Wall Street at Jaw-Dropping Discount
stories.excerpt: Joseph Hoffman’s Bushburg Properties is getting a screaming deal on 60 Wall Street, which last traded hands for over $1 billion in 2017. Bushburg is in contract to purchase the 1.6 million-square-foot office tower in Manhattan’s Financial District for $400 million from Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC, according to The Real Deal. The purchase comes five years after Deutsche Bank vacated the premises in 2021. GIC originally purchased a 95 percent stake in the property from Paramount Group and Morgan Stanley for $1.04 billion in 2017. Paramount became Elecor Properties after being acquired by Rithm Capital in April. GIC sold down its stake in 60 Wall Street over the past few years, and it had between a 45 and 50 percent stake in the property prior to entering the new contract with Bushberg, according to a source close to the deal. Gary Phillips and Will Silverman of Eastdil Secured Savills represented the seller in the transaction, but declined to comment. Bushburg Properties and GIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment. However, Bushburg has an opportunity to convert the former single-tenant headquarters developed in the 1980s by J.P. Morgan Chase into a residential tower. Office-to-residential conversions have been the developer’s specialty. Exactly why the property did not perform well as an office asset is unclear. In fact, the 46-story tower seems to have been an enigma for the industry as a whole going back to 2012, when Commercial Observer reported that brokers and tenants seemed unfamiliar with the asset. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bushburg Properties in contract to buy 60 Wall Street Financial District office tower for $400M from GIC.
1.6M SF property last traded for $1.04B in 2017; 62% decline reflects office market distress.
Deutsche Bank vacated 2021; GIC reducing exposure signals institutional retreat from Manhattan office.
stories.summary: Bushburg Properties is in contract to purchase the 1.6 million-square-foot office tower at 60 Wall Street in Manhattan's Financial District for $400 million from Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC. The property last sold for $1.04 billion in 2017 and has been largely vacant since Deutsche Bank's departure in 2021. GIC is divesting its stake after years of holding the property.
stories.impact: Severe Manhattan office oversupply and value destruction create conversion and repositioning opportunities; expect accelerated office-to-residential conversion pipeline in Financial District and Midtown, potentially expanding multifamily supply in Manhattan core over next 3–5 years. Developers should track distressed office asset sales and entitlement pathways for mixed-use and residential redevelopment; capital willing to take massive losses on office signals desperation and potential regulatory/entitlement tailwinds for residential conversion deals.

stories.title: Brookfield Asset Management Raises $25B Thanks to Infrastructure Investment
stories.excerpt: Thanks to demand for infrastructure projects, investment behemoth Brookfield Asset Management is on its way to breaching its fundraising record this year, having hauled $25 billion in funding in the third quarter, bringing the year-to-date total to $123 billion. Over the past year, the firm, which holds over $1 trillion in assets under management, has raised or received commitments of approximately $50 billion for its infrastructure funds and another $8 billion for its debt fund. The New York-based firm attributed some of its success to remaining a reliant and responsible investor with decades of experience in an otherwise risky and volatile sector driven by speculative data center projects to satisfy demands from artificial intelligence. “Brookfield has been doing large-scale infrastructure for decades. … We don’t take a different approach to AI infrastructure that we take to any other infrastructure asset class,” Connor Teskey, CEO of Brookfield Asset Management, said on a Friday third-quarter earnings call. “We look to de-risk the development, only putting capital in the ground once we’ve secured offtake, equipment supply, and permits. We only build in places where we have long-term community support.” The executive dismissed worries about the broad stock market selloff following the midterm elections earlier this week that saw a slew of anti-AI Democrats elected, saying: “We really don’t see ourselves changing our business model. It’s incredibly robust, incredibly resilient, and still seeing significant demand.” Brookfield Asset Management’s revenue shot up to $2.1 billion in the third quarter, up by 72 percent from the same time last year. Net income grew to just under $3 billion in the third quarter and $5.4 billion over the past year, up from nearly $700 million and $2.5 billion, respectively, from the same periods last year. bullets: Brookfield Asset Management raised $123B year-to-date; $25B in Q3 driven by infrastructure demand.
Firm raised/received $50B commitments for infrastructure funds and $8B for debt funds over past year.
Brookfield emphasizes disciplined infrastructure approach vs. speculative AI data center focus; $1T+ AUM.
stories.summary: Brookfield Asset Management raised $25 billion in Q3 2024, bringing year-to-date fundraising to $123 billion, driven by strong demand for infrastructure projects. Over the past year, the firm mobilized approximately $50 billion in commitments for infrastructure funds and $8 billion for debt funds. Brookfield, with over $1 trillion in assets under management, positioned itself as a disciplined, long-term infrastructure investor distinct from speculative AI data center players.
stories.impact: Capital availability for large-scale, institutional real estate remains robust despite tech sector volatility; Brookfield's infrastructure focus signals flight-to-quality and away from speculative AI bets. Multifamily developers with institutional partnerships and recession-resistant assets will benefit from this capital availability; debt fund growth ($8B) indicates lenders willing to finance residential projects with stable cash flows, supporting development financing costs and availability in strong multifamily markets.

stories.title: Trump Administration Designates 210 Qualified Opportunity Zones in NYC
stories.excerpt: President Donald Trump’s administration designated 6,500 Qualified Opportunity Zones (QOZ) throughout the U.S., with 210 in New York City alone. While the renewal of the Opportunity Zone program has 2,200 fewer QOZs than its original 2016 designations, up to 60 percent of the zones in the city are in Brooklyn and the Bronx, according to the U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). The renewal of the program offering tax benefits to developers working to revitalize underinvested communities comes days after Tuesday’s midterm elections, which marked a setback for the Republican Party that could define the nation’s political dynamics for the next few election cycles. “Under President Trump’s leadership, the Working Families Tax Cuts permanently renewed and strengthened Opportunity Zones, giving investors, entrepreneurs, and local leaders the long-term certainty they need to commit capital to communities that have been overlooked for too long,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. “Today’s announcement of the new designations will help direct private investment to these communities, expand economic opportunity, support job creation, and unlock long-term growth in these communities across the country.” Opportunity Zones are defined geographic areas in which developers can receive tax breaks for undertaking needed development, particularly housing. But tax incentives alone are not enough to get development on the right course to address the national housing shortage, according to Adam Sanders, a real estate attorney at Rosenberg & Estis. “New York has 430 designated zones, with nearly half in New York City. Brooklyn and the Bronx account for most of the city’s designations, so there’s clearly potential for investment in those areas,” Sanders said in a statement. “But a tax incentive alone doesn’t make a project viable. bullets: Trump administration designated 6,500 Qualified Opportunity Zones nationwide; 210 in NYC (60% in Brooklyn/Bronx).
QOZ program renewed with 2,200 fewer zones than original 2016 designations; tax incentives restored.
Brooklyn and Bronx concentration signals targeted incentive for underinvested outer-borough development.
stories.summary: President Trump's administration designated 6,500 Qualified Opportunity Zones across the U.S., including 210 in New York City, with approximately 60% concentrated in Brooklyn and the Bronx. The renewed QOZ program contains 2,200 fewer zones than the original 2016 designations but restores tax benefits for investors committing capital to economically disadvantaged communities.
stories.impact: QOZ renewal creates targeted tax-incentive tailwind for multifamily development in Brooklyn and Bronx submarkets; reduced total zones make NYC designations more valuable and competitive. Developers should prioritize QOZ-eligible sites in outer boroughs (e.g., East Flatbush, Sunset Park, Astoria, Long Island City periphery) to capture capital gains tax deferral and 15% exclusion; expect accelerated acquisition and development activity in these zones through 2027–2029 as investors race to deploy capital before eventual program expiration.
